message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Command Prompt

On Windows you can terminate a running program by its **image name** (the executable file) or by its **process ID (PID)**.  
For VS Code the image name is `code.exe`.

#### 1. Kill *all* VS Code processes by image name

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – specifies the image name (`code.exe`).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “kill -9” on Unix).

This will close every instance of VS Code that is currently running.

#### 2. Kill a specific instance by PID

If you only want to close one particular window, first find its PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

You’ll see output similar to:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
code.exe                   12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
code.exe                   67890 Console                    1     140,000 K
```

Then kill the desired PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

Replace `12345` with the actual PID you wish to terminate.

#### 3. Using PowerShell (optional)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or by PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑close every VS Code instance |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes and their PIDs |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑close a specific VS Code instance |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |
| `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the second command |

**Tip:** If you’re running into “Access denied” errors, try opening the Command Prompt or PowerShell as an administrator.
